notes:
Primary contact: CTO (Ravi Mehta) — building an in-IDE copilot for enterprise dev teams. Key ask: TTFT and steady-state jitter control for streaming completions inside VS Code plugin.

Requirements summary:
- UX targets: first token TTFT <= 120ms (cold), 30-70ms warm; jitter <20ms for subsequent token chunks. 95th percentile targets matter.
- Token budget policies: per-completion token budget (e.g., 64 / 256), hard abort vs soft degrade, ability to cap total monthly tokens per org/workspace.
- Streaming behavior: incremental tokens every 8-16 tokens, partial commit events for editor to render; cancel/replace mid-stream; stable partials so suggestions don't flicker.
- Backpressure & throttling: IDE should signal client priority levels (context completion vs background refactor), platform should drop low-priority batches under load.
- Model/version pinning: want deterministic outputs for tests; ability to pin a model hash and fall back to deterministic quantized variant on capacity constraints.
- Metrics & observability: per-request TTFT, chunk latency histogram, jitter, dropped-chunk counts, token burn per suggestion.
- Deployment: prefer hosted API for initial POC, dedicated or VPC for larger deployments and data residency.

Quotes & shorthand from calls:
- "If TTFT spikes our adoption drops — devs notice sub-200ms instantly." — CTO
- "We need explicit API hooks for token budgets and mid-stream aborts." — Lead Client SDK eng

POC ask: Redwood to run 2-week in-IDE POC with a small sample of power users (20 devs). Need guidance on streaming chunk sizes and recommended token-budget defaults. SE to provide sample config + cost estimate.
